title: Which is cheaper for each gram, the chikki or the chips?
description: A packet of peanut chikki and a packet of potato chips hold different amounts, so the video divides each price by its weight to get the price of one gram, rounds to three places and compares.
teaching_notes: One idea: divide each price by its weight, round the answers to the same number of places, then compare. Ask the class which packet looks cheaper by its price tag before any work is shown. Watch for students who compare the two price tags and ignore the grams.

source: End of chapter Figure it Out, Q1
video_script.why: The child can find the price of one gram for whole number prices, and now meets prices with decimals that do not divide evenly.
video_script.substitution: Each price is divided by its weight, the answers are rounded to three places, and the two prices of one gram are compared.
video_script.anchor: A 210 gram packet of peanut chikki costing 70.5 rupees and a 110 gram packet of potato chips costing 33.25 rupees
video_script.payoff_line: The potato chips are cheaper, at about zero point three zero two rupees for each gram

final_answer.value: The potato chips, about ₹0.302 per gram

maths_rules: chikki: 70.5 ÷ 210 = 7.05 ÷ 21 = 0.3357..., about 0.336 (the fourth place is 7, so round up)
chips: 33.25 ÷ 110 = 3.325 ÷ 11 = 0.3022..., about 0.302 (the fourth place is 2, so keep)
0.302 < 0.336, so the chips are cheaper for each gram
video_script.design: One idea: divide each price by its weight, round to three places and compare. The two packets stay on the board all video; the working band builds in the idea part, one step per packet and then the comparison.

<bookmark mark='chikki'/>A packet of peanut chikki weighs two hundred and ten grams. It costs seventy point five rupees.
<bookmark mark='chips'/>A packet of potato chips weighs one hundred and ten grams. It costs thirty three point two five rupees.
Which is cheaper?

narration: <bookmark mark='why'/>Step one, find the price of one gram of chikki.
<bookmark mark='div'/>Divide seventy point five by two hundred and ten.
<bookmark mark='ten'/>Divide both numbers by ten, to get seven point zero five divided by twenty one.
<bookmark mark='long'/>Long division gives zero point three three five seven, and more digits follow.
<bookmark mark='round'/>The fourth digit is seven, so the third digit goes up by one. One gram of chikki costs about zero point three three six rupees.

marks.why: the step title and the chips packet are lit
marks.ten: both numbers are divided by 10 to give 3.325 ÷ 11

narration: <bookmark mark='why'/>Step two, find the price of one gram of chips.
<bookmark mark='div'/>Divide thirty three point two five by one hundred and ten.
<bookmark mark='ten'/>Divide both numbers by ten, to get three point three two five divided by eleven.
<bookmark mark='long'/>Long division gives zero point three zero two two, and more digits follow.
<bookmark mark='round'/>The fourth digit is two, so the third digit stays. One gram of chips costs about zero point three zero two rupees.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: compare the prices of 1 g: 0.302 < 0.336

<bookmark mark='less'/>Zero point three zero two is less than zero point three three six.
